main_text.head: ΟΠΙΣΤΟΓΡΑΦΙΑ
AD OXONIENSES.
main_text.p: CIO SI QVID REActe in humanis rebus geratur, nulla esse hominis peculiarem, propriamq; laudem, at unius duntaxat Dei: A quo, ceu perenni fonte, universa haec, in nobis, recte agendi tum facultas, tum voluntas proficiscitur. Attamen quoniam uel organa ipsa plerunq;, ac instrumenta, per quae opes, in nos, suas transfundit Deus, amplecti ac magnificare consueuimus: Equidem inter caeteras Christianae Reip. scholas, nō in postremo humanae commendationis loco Academiā uestram (Oxonienses) collocandā duxerim. Vnde tot tantaq; bona, orbi Christiano, peperit caelestis prouidentia. Quanquam haec (ut dixi, iterumq; admoneo) nō loco, sed diuina benignitate metienda sunt. Neq; enim tanto pere refert, quid quo loco accipimus, sed quid hoc ipsum sit, quantaq; rei magnitudo spectandum est. Quis satis reputando aestimare poterit immensam, ac ineffabilem huius beneficii

page.notes: The initial S is a large woodcut letter, joined to "CIO" as "SCIO" in the text. The word "beneficii" is partly obscured at the line end and "huius" is partly obscured; the reading is uncertain. The line "CIO SI QVID" reads as printed with the initial. The Greek title is printed in Greek letters as shown. Show-through from the reverse page is present at the top and was omitted.
